headline: Van Veen builds 6-2 lead and sees off Schindler 10-7
standfirst: Gian van Veen averaged 101.69 and survived a late Martin Schindler rally to reach the Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals.
body: Gian van Veen booked a place in the Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals with a 10-7 win over Martin Schindler in the last 16 at Wolverhampton on Thursday. The Dutchman averaged 101.69 to Schindler’s 99.51.

Schindler took the opening leg, but van Veen won four of the next five legs to lead 4-2 and then took the next two to go 6-2 clear. Three breaks of throw along the way helped him into a 9-3 lead, and the match appeared to be over as a contest.

Schindler had other ideas. He won four legs in a row, including two breaks of throw and a 10-dart leg, to cut the gap to 9-7. He hit six 180s to van Veen’s four, but missed too many doubles: his checkout rate was 28 per cent, against 37.04 for his opponent.
Van Veen did not let the comeback go further. He broke the Schindler throw in 11 darts, finishing on 93, to complete the win. He had broken throw five times in all.
He now plays Nathan Aspinall in the quarter-finals on Saturday evening.
